📌 Blind Signing: Why Approving What You Can’t Read Is Dangerous

Main Points
⏺ Your wallet sometimes asks you to sign data it cannot decode
⏺ You see a hash or raw hex instead of clear actions
⏺ This post explains why blind signing is risky and how to avoid it


1⃣ Core Idea — Blind signing means approving a transaction or message without a readable summary of what it actually does.
2⃣ Why It Exists — Some smart contracts are complex, and hardware wallets or apps can’t always parse them, so they show only a hash.
3⃣ Example — You expect to claim a reward, but the hidden payload is a token approval or a transfer of your NFTs to someone else.
4⃣ Risk Surface — Phishing sites rely on this: once you sign, the transaction is valid and usually can’t be reversed.
5⃣ Practical Rule — Keep blind signing off by default, use wallets with transaction simulation, and never sign on a site you reached from a DM or ad.
Final Thoughts

A signature is not a formality — it is your consent. If your wallet can’t tell you what you’re approving, assume the worst and stop.

🌐 BlackRock sees record Bitcoin whale demand for IBIT conversions despite ETF outflows 

⚠️ BlackRock has reported record demand from large Bitcoin holders seeking to convert their cryptocurrency into shares of its iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), with security concerns driving approximately $3.6 billion in reported transactions. According to Robbie Mitchnick, BlackRock’s head of digital assets, demand for in-kind Bitcoin conversions has continued growing despite recent cryptocurrency price declines. Speaking to Barron’s on November 9, Mitchnick said investors increasingly prefer holding Bitcoin exposure through regulated investment products instead of managing large cryptocurrency balances themselves. 

🚫 The actual amount may be higher because BlackRock does not directly process or track every transaction completed through its intermediaries. Mitchnick described current interest as “the highest we’ve seen at any point”, pointing to continued demand among wealthy individuals and institutional Bitcoin holders. He identified “security and peace of mind” as the main reasons investors request the service, particularly those seeking alternatives to managing private keys and maintaining large cryptocurrency balances in personal wallets.

➡️ Through in-kind conversions, eligible investors transfer existing Bitcoin into the ETF structure and receive shares representing their investment. The transactions involve authorized participants and other approved intermediaries responsible for arranging the creation of ETF shares. BlackRock works with firms including Galaxy Digital, Talos and Virtu to facilitate conversions, while minimum transaction requirements depend on the intermediary.

Political Earthquake : Democrats Have Clawed Back  Control Over Mississippi 🌪️

In a stunning political upset, Democrat Scott Colom has defeated Republican incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi’s U.S. Senate race, delivering a major blow to the Republican Party in one of America’s most traditionally conservative states.

Colom, a 43-year-old prosecutor, secured approximately 49.2% of the vote, narrowly defeating Hyde-Smith, who received 48.7%. The Associated Press called the race on November 11 after days of uncertainty and the counting of outstanding ballots. Hyde-Smith subsequently conceded.

The victory is historic for another reason. Colom will become Mississippi’s first Black U.S. senator since Reconstruction, marking a significant moment in the state’s political history.

The result is particularly striking given Trump’s strong support for Hyde-Smith and his personal efforts to encourage Mississippi voters to keep the Republican senator in Washington.

Colom’s campaign focused heavily on issues affecting ordinary Americans, including rising living costs, wages, healthcare access and the future of rural communities.

His message appears to have resonated with voters who wanted a change in representation.

The outcome also adds to a difficult election cycle for Republicans. Democrats are celebrating the result as evidence that even traditionally reliable Republican territory can become politically competitive.

For the GOP, the loss raises difficult questions about voter dissatisfaction, campaign strategy and the limits of presidential influence in local elections.

But the bigger story may be what happens next. With control of Congress at stake, every Senate seat carries enormous political weight.
Mississippi has sent Washington a message that few political observers expected. 

Whether this victory signals a broader transformation in American politics remains to be seen.

🌐 Former FBI agent pleads guilty to stealing $2.47M in crypto from 35 investigations 

🔔 Former FBI agent Patrick Steven Yaroch has pleaded guilty to wire fraud and money laundering after stealing approximately $2.47 million in cryptocurrency through nearly 100 unauthorized transfers linked to 35 federal investigations. Yaroch, who previously worked in the bureau’s counterintelligence division, faces a maximum sentence of 20 years in prison. U.S. District Judge Patricia Tolliver Giles accepted his guilty plea in Alexandria, Virginia, with sentencing scheduled for March 4, 2027.

📊 Court documents show that Yaroch worked at the FBI’s Boston Division between 2017 and early 2025, where he was assigned to a squad investigating an adversarial nation-state. He subsequently transferred to the Counterintelligence and Espionage Division in February 2025, gaining access to FBI systems containing cryptocurrency credentials obtained during criminal and intelligence investigations. 

⚡️ Prosecutors said his thefts began no later than December 2024, before he moved to the new division. Using credentials associated with investigations outside his authorized activities, Yaroch accessed cryptocurrency wallets and transferred funds without permission. The approximately 100 fraudulent transactions involved credentials connected to 35 separate FBI investigations. Authorities calculated his total illicit proceeds at $2,474,380.66, substantially exceeding the roughly $1 million initially identified when his activities became public.

Few American coins are tied as closely to the Civil War as the 1861-O double eagle, a $20 gold piece from the New Orleans Mint.

The mint worked for the United States until January 26, 1861, when Louisiana seceded. The state took it over, and then the Confederacy.

Of the 17,741 coins struck that year, the generally accepted breakdown credits 5,000 to the federal government, 9,750 to the state of Louisiana and 2,991 to the Confederate States of America. Because every one was made with a single pair of dies, no one can tell which government struck any particular coin.

In October 2026, an 1861-O double eagle graded AU53 by PCGS, from the Christensen Family Collection, sold at Heritage Auctions for $91,500.
